name: Crindau House
summary: Substantial Tudor regional stone house, representing the ancient agrarian manor that preceded Crindau's industrial surge.

name: Newport Gas Company (Crindau Works)
summary: Expansive municipal works and chemical by-product plant situated at the bottom of Albany Street alongside the railway and river.

name: South Wales Glass Works
summary: Major local employer reflected heavily in Albany Street directory entries for glassblowers, stokers, and packers.

name: G.F. Lovell & Co. Confectionery Works
summary: Prominent toffee and sweet manufacturer (famous for Milky Lunch and Rexville), employing generations of local families.

name: Rexville (Lovells Athletic FC)
summary: The home ground of the confectionery works' team, drawing huge crowds for Southern League and Welsh Cup ties.

name: Newport Smelting Works
summary: Specialist non-ferrous and copper smelting operations taking advantage of the rail links and coastal tidal wharves.

name: Crindau Infants & Junior School
summary: Built by the Newport School Board to serve the rapid population boom of railwaymen, gasworkers, and industrial labourers.
